title.rendered: Declaring Over Your Body: By His Stripes | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 7

excerpt.rendered: By His stripes, healing is already purchased. Day 7 teaches believers how to declare over the body, not against medicine, but with the finished work of Jesus.

content.rendered:
Jesus did not come to leave healing for one day a year or one special service a month. By His stripes, it is already purchased. Declaration is how a believer takes delivery.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, October 24, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 7

Today’s Scripture

“But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities; the chastisement for our peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed.”
Isaiah 53:5 (NKJV)

“Who Himself bore our sins in His own body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live for righteousness, by whose stripes you were healed.”
1 Peter 2:24 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

There is a reason Peter quotes Isaiah 53:5 in the perfect tense. The NKJV says, “by whose stripes you were healed.” The AMPC reinforces it: “By His wounds you have been healed.” The TPT is beautiful: “His wounds became your healing.” Jesus is not going to heal, healing is already in His blood, written into the stripes He carried on His back. The believer’s role is not to beg heaven for what Calvary already secured. The believer’s role is to agree with heaven about what Calvary already secured.

This matters pastorally, because sickness is cruel. From Lagos, where a father paces outside an emergency ward, to London, where a diaspora grandmother waits for scan results, to Manila, where a child is still fighting a fever that will not break, to Nairobi and São Paulo, where ministries pray on hospital stairs, the question is never whether we care; it is whether we know what Christ has done. Declaration over the body is not a denial of symptoms. It is agreement with the finished work of Jesus while symptoms are still speaking. Use the doctors. Take the medicine. And keep speaking what Scripture says over the body.

Jesus modelled this gently and firmly. He spoke to fevers (Luke 4:39). He said to the paralytic, “Arise, take up your bed, and walk” (John 5:8). He told the woman with the issue of blood that her faith had made her well (Mark 5:34). He laid hands on people and let the power of the Holy Spirit flow, but He also opened His mouth and said what the Father said. Healing in the Gospels almost always has a sentence attached.

So decree it. Over your body, over the body of your spouse, over your children, over the sick saints in your church. Speak the Word gently, respectfully, consistently. Thank Him for what is already finished. Address what is in your body in the name of Jesus, as Jesus Himself did. And remember, if the breath of God framed worlds, the Word of God can refurbish a weary human body.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. Healing is already purchased. Isaiah 53:5 happened before you were sick. Peter wrote it in the perfect tense for a reason.

Personalise. Lay a hand on your head, your chest, your knee, wherever symptoms are speaking. Address your body as something God made and loves. Call it by what Scripture calls it.

Proclaim. Speak gently and firmly. “By His stripes I am healed.” “Life, in the name of Jesus.” Keep speaking across the hours of the day, not only in a moment of crisis.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that by the stripes of Jesus, I am healed. His wounds became my healing. I am not begging for what Calvary already purchased. I speak life to my body, from the crown of my head to the soles of my feet. Every system in my body (immune, circulatory, nervous, hormonal, respiratory, digestive), hear the word of the Lord and align with the design of the Creator and the finished work of the Redeemer. Pain, I resist you in Jesus’ name. Disease, you have no right where the blood of Jesus has already settled the matter. My body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and the Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead lives in me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
